label: g1_ledger
name: Liquid-coupled slip stack
mech: In a 10 mm bend strip, the bonded OCA is replaced by a sealed, index-matched fluid film. This lets the UTG, the touch/polarizer layer and the OLED-on-PI each bend about their own neutral plane, so ε ≈ 30 µm/(2×2 mm) ≈ 0.75% instead of about 4% for a bonded stack. Outside the strip, the layers stay bonded with normal OCA. The closest attempt, thin or high-recovery OCA, failed because it stays bonded and so stays strained; a fluid has no shape memory. The deciding quantity is whether the perimeter seal holds the fluid gap uniform to within ±1 µm through 2000 cycles at 45 °C.
value: Removes the creeping layer itself rather than reducing its creep.

label: g1_ledger
name: Tensioned drumhead hinge
mech: In the last few degrees of opening, the hinge cams pull the panel edges outward, applying a measured in-plane membrane tension that elastically pulls any residual dent flat. Load cells in the hinge store the tension that gives zero slope and adapt it with temperature. The closest attempts, perforated plates and the Oppo-mapped hinge, only support the panel from below, and supports cannot remove the panel's own set. The deciding quantity is the tension needed to flatten a 20 µm, 3 mm-wide set compared with the OCA edge-shear creep limit.
value: Flatness becomes an actively controlled state rather than a material hope.

label: g1_ledger
name: Post-shakedown counter-shaped support
mech: Each panel is first aged in the factory with about 300 hot folds until its crease depth saturates. Its residual profile is then laser-mapped at 0.3 µm, and a matching inverse shim is printed onto the support plate. The closest attempt, Oppo's liquid printing, maps the surface before use, while the creep has not happened yet. Here the mapping happens after the creep has stopped. The deciding quantity is whether depth drift between cycle 300 and cycle 2300 stays ≤2 µm under 60 °C folded holds.
value: Cancels the stable part of the crease while reusing existing Oppo-style tooling.

label: g1_neg
name: Fold-native polymer lamination
mech: The OCA and polyimide layers are laminated while the panel is held at its fold radius. Their stress-free shape is therefore the folded state, so the long hours folded in a pocket cause no creep. When the phone is open, the polymers try to re-curl, but the stress-free flat glass and the plate are much stiffer and hold the panel flat. The closest earlier attempt is neutral-plane balancing, which is tuned for one state and still creeps; here the creep-prone layers spend their long holds at zero stress. The deciding quantity is the polymer's relaxing moment compared with the bending stiffness of the glass plus plate, which must be at least 50× larger to keep depth under 2 µm.
value: It removes the cause of the crease instead of repairing its effect, at near-zero material cost.

label: g1_neg
name: Drumhead tension hinge
mech: A cam in the hinge slides both panel ends outward on opening and applies about 600 N/m of in-plane tension. This pulls any set curvature down onto a flat lapped support plate. With UTG bending stiffness of about 1.6×10⁻⁴ N·m, flattening decays over √(D/T) ≈ 0.5 mm, while the glass strain stays at about 0.03%. The closest earlier attempt is Oppo's tolerance fill, which is static and cannot follow creep; tension adapts automatically as the set grows. The deciding quantity is roughly 90 N of sustained hinge force without causing OCA shear delamination.
value: Flatness is restored on every opening, whatever creep has accumulated.

label: g1_neg
name: Closed-loop active fold support
mech: A row of about 30 piezo or wedge actuators under the fold zone has about 60 µm of stroke and 1 µm resolution. Strain gauges printed on the polyimide estimate the crease profile at each opening, and a stored map drives the actuators to cancel it. The map is updated as creep grows. The closest earlier attempt is Oppo's laser-mapped liquid printing, a one-time static fill that cannot track drift. The deciding quantity is whether the panel's bending stiffness lets discrete supports cancel slope below 0.5 mrad between actuators.
value: Flatness is held under 2 µm across temperature, humidity and wear by measuring and correcting it, not by hoping the materials recover.

label: g1_mech
name: Sub-creep strain budget fold
mech: The hinge holds the bend zone at a radius of at least 5 mm. This is done with a deep teardrop cavity, with the panel sliding into each half on rails, so the closed phone stays about 10 mm thick. The panel stack in the bend zone is thinned to about 60 µm of polymer, so peak strain stays at or below 0.3–0.5%, under the yield and creep onset of polyimide and adhesive at 60 °C. The closest earlier attempt is the teardrop hinge, which stopped near R = 1.5–2 mm and therefore stayed in the creep regime. Translating the panel into the halves lifts the thickness cap that stopped it. The deciding quantity is the residual strain after an 8 h hold at 60 °C in the worst layer, which must be at or below 0.05%.
value: Any crease that remains is elastic and recovers fully, giving a fold whose flatness can be certified rather than merely improved.

label: g1_mech
name: Unbonded sliding bend-zone laminate
mech: Across the 15 mm bend zone, the glass, OLED-on-polyimide and support plate are left unbonded. They are separated by a sealed index-matched silicone fluid film (n ≈ 1.47, about 5 µm thick) and bonded only outside the zone. Each layer then bends about its own neutral axis, so strain is t_i/2R: about 0.75% for 30 µm glass and 0.5% for 20 µm polyimide at R = 2 mm. No adhesive shear creep can lock in a dent. The closest earlier attempt is low-modulus, high-recovery adhesive, which still couples the layers and creeps under heat and humidity. This design removes the adhesive from the bend zone entirely. The deciding quantity is fluid retention and edge-seal integrity over 2,000 cycles, measured as gap uniformity within ±0.5 µm.
value: The polymer creep that sets every shipped crease is removed without adding thickness.

label: g1_mech
name: Tensioned glass flattening hinge
mech: When the phone opens, cam-driven sliders in the hinge put the display under in-plane tension, about 20–40 N/m. The hinge also overbends about 2° past flat before settling. A force sensor stores the residual-curvature history and adjusts the overbend over the device's life. Tension reduces out-of-plane waviness in proportion to the residual bending moment divided by the tension. Because the glass is elastic, it returns the stack to flat as long as the polymer set stays small. The closest earlier attempt is Oppo's one-time laser mapping and liquid fill, which is static and cannot track creep that develops later. This design corrects on every cycle. The deciding quantity is the tension needed to reach 5 µm compared with the edge-flaw strength of the glass.
value: The crease is held at zero throughout the device's life, so slow creep in the field never becomes visible.

label: g1_rf1
name: Glass-dominated elastic fold zone
mech: Two 30 µm UTG sheets enclose the OLED, joined by ≤10 µm low-modulus OCA across the fold zone only. More than 99% of the bending moment is then carried by glass that cannot creep, and the residual curvature scales with the polymer's moment share. The closest attempt is SDC Advanced Crease-less with a possible second UTG, which still leaves a thick PI/OCA stack bearing load. This design removes that load path. The deciding quantity is the polymer moment fraction times its unrecovered creep strain, which must give ≤0.5 mrad slope.
value: An inward book-fold phone whose open-state flatness is set by elastic glass instead of creeping polymer.

label: g1_rf1
name: Hinge reverse-bend creep cancellation
mech: On opening, the hinge briefly over-extends 2–4° past flat, then settles at 180°. The reverse bend applies a counter-moment that, by Boltzmann superposition, cancels the stored viscoelastic creep from the folded hold. The dwell time adapts to the logged closed time and temperature. The closest attempt is neutral-plane balancing, which suits only one state, and this approach adds the missing second state. The deciding quantity is the reverse strain-time needed against a 72 h folded hold at 60 °C.
value: Turns accumulated polymer creep from a permanent dent into a cancelled transient without adding layers.

label: g1_rf1
name: Tensioned membrane open state
mech: In the flat state, hinge cams pull the wing plates apart, putting the fold-zone stack in in-plane tension. The tension straightens residual curvature: deflection falls as tension rises relative to bending stiffness. The closest attempt is Oppo's tolerance-mapped hinge, which fills gaps but applies no restoring force. The deciding quantity is the tension needed for ≤1 µm depth against OCA shear-creep and UTG edge stress limits.
value: Actively flattens whatever crease the materials leave, while reusing hinge parts that phones already have.

label: g1_rf2
name: Gel-slip decoupled glass stack
mech: In the fold band, the OCA is replaced by an index-matched, sealed silicone gel or fluid that carries the 157 µm interlayer slip as flow with no shape memory. Each solid layer then bends about its own midplane at ε = t/2R ≤ 1%. This differs from creep-recovery OCAs, which still store shear; the deciding quantity is the gel's residual shear set after 8 h folded at 60 °C. The polarizer is replaced by colour-filter-on-encapsulation, which cuts layer separation by about 50 µm.
value: It removes the layer that dominates crease formation, so a crease cannot form under worst-case dwell.

label: g1_rf2
name: OLED directly on UTG
mech: The TFT and OLED are built on a 30 µm strengthened glass substrate instead of PI, and the panel is sealed with a second UTG. Only glass carries strain, at 0.75% for R = 2 mm. Glass shows no creep at room temperature, so there is no material that can take a permanent set. This differs from earlier thick-UTG covers, which still sat on PI and OCA that creep. The deciding quantity is the 2000-cycle fatigue survival of glass at 0.75% strain with TFT films on it.
value: Every load-bearing layer stays fully elastic, which makes crease persistence a non-issue.

label: g1_rf2
name: Large-radius tensioning teardrop hinge
mech: A teardrop hinge with R ≥ 3 mm keeps every bonded layer below 0.3% strain. On opening, sliding wing plates put the panel under about 0.1% in-plane tension, pulling any residual curvature flat against a continuous, interlocking plate. This differs from current teardrop hinges, which leave the panel slack and depend on hinge tolerance. The deciding quantity is the residual depth under tension after dwell, versus the tension the edge bonds can hold.
value: It actively flattens the panel each time it opens, using shipped materials, at a cost of about 1.5 mm more folded thickness.

label: repair
name: Glass-tendon tensioned clothoid hinge
mech: The anchor is kept: when the phone opens, the panel is put under in-plane tension that pulls any residual curvature flat. The tension now goes through the 45 µm UTG alone. Titanium rails grip the glass's two outer edges, and a force-controlled flexure spring, latched by a cam in the last few degrees of opening, sets the load at T ≈ 2000 N/m. That is 44 MPa in the glass, 0.063% strain and 300 N in total. A soft silicone optical gel (G ≈ 2 kPa) replaces the acrylic OCA under the glass. Through the acrylic OCA only 30% of the tension reached the fold, at about 48 kPa sustained shear. Through the gel 97% reaches it, at 1.9 kPa. The hinge path changes from a sharp teardrop to a teardrop with R = 3 mm and clothoid curvature ramps of at least 2 mm. Without the ramps, features narrower than √(D/T) ≈ 0.57 mm cannot be pulled flat. In a beam-column model with plate contact, calibrated so that today's creases come out at 60–150 µm, the result is a crease ≤2.1 µm deep with slope ≤0.82 mrad. The targets are ≤5 µm and ≤1 mrad. This holds for any untensioned crease up to about 180 µm.
value: The cost is an estimated $13–50 per phone that meets the spec, about 16–72% of a $70–80 hinge. The reported baselines (Fold 7, Apple/Samsung Display drilled plate, Oppo N6) deliver essentially no phones that meet a ≤5 µm / ≤1 mrad spec, so no meaningful cost ratio exists.

label: repair
name: Per-layer sub-creep strain budget
mech: The anchor is kept: every polymer layer in the bend zone stays below its measured no-set strain, so no crease forms in the first place. The budget is now set per layer, not for the whole stack. With soft interlayers, each layer bends about its own mid-plane, so its strain is t_i/2R. The kill test's "60 µm stack at R = 5 mm = 0.6%" therefore does not apply. The thickest polymer layer is capped at 25 µm: the PET protector is removed, the UTG is hard-coated, and the back film is 25 µm CPI. The OCA is a low-relaxation silicone, because OCA slip (πd/2) does not shrink with radius. The locked shear drops from 92 kPa (acrylic) to 6 kPa. The polymers' share of bending stiffness falls from 16.9% to 2.4%. The hinge sets R ≥ 4.2 mm, which gives 0.30% per layer and about a 10.2 mm spine at the hinge.
value: Any crease that remains is elastic and recovers, so flatness can be certified. The estimated cost is $7–33 per phone that meets the spec, about 8–47% of the hinge cost, plus about 1.3 mm more thickness than the 8.9 mm Fold 7.

label: repair
name: Floating glass on fluid
mech: Anchor kept: an index-matched liquid film, not an adhesive, couples the ultra-thin glass (UTG) to the panel where it bends. Because a liquid has no shape memory, the visible surface sits on a layer that cannot take a set. The repair fixes the flaw the kill test found: wherever the liquid strip met bonded adhesive, the layers had to slip 157 µm past each other, a shear strain of 6.3 against the 2.5–4 that folding adhesives are designed for. So the fluid (20 µm of phenyl-silicone, refractive index 1.51 ±0.02, viscosity 0.05–0.1 Pa·s) now covers the whole display, and the 149 µm of slip at each edge runs out at the perimeter. There it is taken by a pinned meniscus plus a 5 µm polyimide loop seal, which pushes back with at most 0.1 N/m; the glass would buckle at 0.34 N/m. The rest of the stack: 30 µm UTG with no polymer film on top (a bonded 5 µm hardcoat would print a 10 µm crease); a polarizer-free colour-filter OLED panel with touch built in; adhesive plus a 30 µm laser-patterned titanium plate; and a waterdrop hinge with a 3 mm minimum radius, so the glass and panel strain is 0.50% instead of 2.5% for a bonded stack. With the glass free to slip, any set in the layers below is levelled out by fluid flow in 5–10 s. Gravity, heat and stylus effects all stay inside their limits (a gravity tilt of at most 0.27 mrad, a 1.2 µm dome over 140 mm across 60 K, interface reflectance below 10⁻⁴). An earlier round with spacer pillars and a slight vacuum failed: the glass could then sag 360 µm into any dip and the crease printed straight through, so that version was dropped.
value: It removes the layer that creeps from under the viewed surface for an estimated +$2–6 per phone, against roughly +$5–15 (my estimate) for the Apple/Samsung patterned plate or Oppo's ~20-pass printed hinge. On paper it is the only one of these aimed at zero crease rather than a smaller one, so cost per crease-free phone delivered is finite against undefined for the baselines.

label: repair
name: Spectrum-matched drumhead hinge
mech: Anchor kept: on opening, a hinge cam puts in-plane tension on the display and pulls any set flat over a flat plate. That tension works as a long-wavelength filter: the residual is w = w₀·k²/(k² + T/D), so it beats wide sets and loses to narrow ones. I reproduced the kill result (a 20 µm × 3 mm set leaves 3.3 µm and 2.3 mrad at 600 N/m; flattening it needs 3.9 kN/m). At today's 1.5 mm radius, 9.6–56 kN/m would be needed, which no phone can take. So the repair moves the design to where the anchor is strong. A thick hinge spine with a 4–5 mm bend radius spreads the set over a ~9 mm width. At the design tension of 1000 N/m (150 N total), the residual is ≤1 µm and ≤0.5 mrad as long as the set stays below 2.1–3.7% of the fold curvature. Clamping every layer together at the panel ends means the tension never passes through the adhesive as shear: shear in the viewing area drops from the kill's 25 kPa to 9.4 kPa, against a 10.5 kPa creep-test stress. A titanium frame and a 1 mm-stroke constant-force spring keep the tension within ±2% from −20 to +40 °C (±8% with aluminium). Glass strain from the tension is only 0.04%, and the cam releases the tension before folding starts.
value: It turns any set below about 2.5% of the fold curvature into an invisible one, adding about +$8–20 per phone (cam, springs, titanium frame) and about 3 mm of spine thickness. Today's phones sit near 8% by my rough estimate, and the best current alternatives reduce the crease rather than remove it.
